alternative_findings: Costal cartilage and sternal calcification/ossification (not CAC)

Markedly elevated left hemidiaphragm with a large, distended gas-filled stomach underneath that has an air-fluid level and extends high into the left hemithorax (eventration vs large hiatal/paraesophageal hernia)

Irregular soft-tissue density with spiculated-looking margins at the left lower lobe/diaphragmatic dome near the left hilum (slices ~34-39), probably partial volume of the elevated hemidiaphragm, but a left lower lobe lesion cannot be excluded
No definite aortic valve, mitral annular or thoracic aortic wall calcification identified
result.reasoning: I read all 74 contiguous slices, from caudal to cranial. Slices 0-15 show the upper abdomen and liver dome, slices ~16-38 the cardiac ventricles and AV grooves, slices ~39-44 the aortic root and left main region, and the slices above that the great vessels and thoracic inlet. In the lower and mid heart slices (about 16-38), the myocardium and blood pool look uniformly gray. I did not see a definite bright focus along the right AV groove (RCA), the mid/distal anterior interventricular groove or the distal left AV groove (LCx). At the level of the aortic root and pulmonary trunk (slices 40-42), there are small, sharply bright, bone-density foci just left of the aortic root, between the root, the pulmonary trunk and the left atrium. This is the course of the left main and proximal LAD. Slices 40 and 41 each show two small foci, one more anterior-lateral (proximal LAD) and one more posterior (LM/bifurcation). Slice 42 shows one residual fleck. Nothing is seen on slice 39 or 43. The deposits follow across 3 consecutive slices and are consistent with coronary calcium rather than noise. They are small, discrete and punctate rather than dense or continuous. No other coronary territory is involved. Overall this is limited calcium in the LM/proximal LAD, so I rated it MILD (estimated Agatston 1-100). It is borderline with low-moderate because two separate foci are seen across 3 slices. Incidental findings include costal cartilage and sternal calcification. There is also a markedly elevated left hemidiaphragm with a large distended stomach beneath it; distinguishing eventration from a hernia is not certain on these slices.
